source.title: Do deep nets really need weight decay and dropout?

record.tranche_reason: Ablates weight decay and dropout and compares test accuracy under different data-augmentation conditions, testing V6 with a different experimental setup.
record.gate_note: The text reports qualitative test-accuracy comparisons and two percentage-point differences; exact bar values in Figure 1 are not stated in the text.
record.test_reason: This is an original source for V6's augmentation qualification: it measures test accuracy after removing weight decay and dropout together from All-CNN and WRN.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: in the tested convolutional object-recognition settings, sufficient data augmentation can provide the generalization benefits of weight decay and dropout together. The authors qualify this conclusion and call for testing more architectures and datasets.
record.recipe_differences: The study follows some ideas and procedures from Zhang et al. (2017), but tests removal of weight decay and dropout in All-CNN and WRN using image data augmentation.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported comparison varies architecture, dataset, and data-augmentation scheme; the text specifically notes a slightly higher unregularized WRN result on CIFAR-100 with heavier augmentation.
record.problems: Exact Figure 1 accuracy values are not given in the text. The authors state that hyperparameters were inherited from original papers and may not be optimal after regularizer removal; they also note that further work across more architectures and datasets is needed.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1 also plots comparisons across architectures, datasets, and augmentation levels, but the supplied text does not state their individual values or outcomes beyond the comparisons recorded above.

untested.parts: Natural-label versus random-label fitting and held-out performance.
Generalization as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and sensitivity to tuning.
Batch-size effects and remedies under controlled training budgets.
Dropout's isolated effect, fully connected classifiers, very small training sets, and underfitting from excessive dropout. Weight decay and dropout are removed together.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus randomly selected examples.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels are assigned because this study is an original source for V6. Row states refer to V6's joint-removal qualification. Additional Figure 1 comparisons are already declared in rows_left_out; their individual values cannot be recovered from the supplied text. The authors' insignificance statement is not accompanied by statistical testing or uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not compare fitting natural labels with fitting random labels.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold is reported.
No fully connected versus convolutional comparison is reported.
No adaptive optimizer comparison is reported.
The study removes weight decay and dropout together, so their separate effects are not isolated; the text does not give exact accuracy values for the plotted comparisons.
No sharpness or generalization-measure comparison is reported.
No memorized-example removal experiment is reported.
